messages.subject: [statnet_help] Problem using matrix with continuous values as edgecov term
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Problem using matrix with continuous values as edgecov term
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to run an ERGM with valued edge attributes in an edgecov term,
but get the following warning mesage after the model has converged (just
listing one, but this warning repeats 50+ times):

1: In m[tl[!nal] + (hl[!nal] - 1) * network.size(x)] <- val[!nal] :
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

This is the model I'm running:

model3<-ergm(net ~ edgecov(s0) + edges + ttriple+ mutual + isolates +
edgecov(DTC_H1a_mul10,attrname="DTC_H1a_mul1z"), eval.loglik=TRUE,
MCMC.burnin=3000, MCMC.interval=2000, MCMC.samplesize=1000, MCMC.maxit=40,
control=control.ergm(MCMLE.steplength=.25, seed=100))

So you have a general context, my model is examining leadership networks by
using trait configurations between members (the edgecov term) to predict
(directed) leadership ties.

Some information about my model:

1) I'm using a structural zero matrix with my data because my network is
really a collection of many smaller teams who do not interact
2) If I run this model without the edgecov term, it runs just fine
3) The edgecov term I'm trying to use represents the degree to which
personality profiles of two nodes are favorable (e.g., the receiver of the
tie has high extraversion and the sender of the tie has high
agreeableness). The "DTC_H1a_mul1z" edge attributes weight each edge
accordingly. These attributes are attached to the DTC_H1a_mul10 network,
which is simply a matrix with all possible ties between nodes represented.
This way, the edgecov term has all possible edge values for the network. (I
did this based off advice I read elsewhere about edgecov)

Can anyone explain what is going wrong? As part of my troubleshooting, I've
tried dichotoming the DTC_H1a_mul1z matrix and just using that as the
edgecov term, and that worked just fine. I've also checked that my net and
DTC_H1a_mul10 matrices have the same number of nodes, as well as trying
some transformations on my edge values to make them more (or less) extreme.
This makes me feel like my issue must specifically be with how I'm trying
to use my valued data rather than the actual values.

Any and all suggestions are appreciated! I've spent quite a while trying to
figure out what is causing this problem, but I seem to have hit a wall.
Also, I am new to this board, so if there is any additional information I
should be providing about this issue, please let me know.

Thanks,

Sam Holland
Doctoral Candidate, George Mason University

messages.subject: [statnet_help] trouble working with set.edge.attribute()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jesse,


I believe that the problem in your example is that you are trying to set 
the edge values using the wrong function for the shape of your input 
data.  There are two functions for setting the values edge attributes of 
a network:

set.edge.value()  sets the values from a matrix input , and maps the 
elements of the matrix to the corresponding edges (if they exist)

set.edge.attribute() sets the values from a vector input, where each 
element of the vector is mapped to the edge with the corresponding edge id.

It warned you that something was wrong with the "Inappropriate edge 
value" error.  Looks like you 'fixed' it by c(pp), which effectively 
unwrapped the pp matrix into a long vector to avoid the error ... but 
then the elements no longer match up to the correct edges.

I expect that your code will work if you change to set.edge.value(), but
bellow may be a more efficient way to set up your networks:

# create the valued matrix
mat<-matrix(c(0,5,0,3,0,
               5,0,2,1,0,
               0,2,0,3,3,

messages.subject: [statnet_help] help with ergm.count
messages.body_plain:
Hello, Iris,

> I am working with weighted network data and would very much like to
> use ergm.count in my analyses. I am not sure how to use the form
> object properly, and I am getting an error: 'Error: The term sum does
> not exist for this type of ERGM. Are you sure you have the right
> name??.  I get the same error for the nonzero value. I am able to run
> ergm without weights (or at least I think it ignores weights without
> specifying the form object!) using:
> 
> > dat=read.csv(file.choose(),header=TRUE,row.names=1,check.names=FALSE)
> > m=as.matrix(dat)
> >net=network(m,matrix.type="adjacency",directed=FALSE,ignore.eval=FALSE,names.eval="value") 
> >nodeInfo<-read.csv(?Attribute.csv", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE, row.names=1)
> >dat2=as.network(net, vertex.attr=nodeInfo, directed=FALSE, edge.lwd=net%e%'value')

Take a look at the first section of this tutorial for how to set edge
values in network:
https://statnet.csde.washington.edu/trac/attachment/wiki/Sunbelt2013/Valued.pdf .

> >dat2 %v% "Sex"<-nodeInfo$Sex #Similar thing done for all attributes I am interested in using in my model
> >model<-ergm(dat2~edges+nodematch('Sex', diff=FALSE)+nodecov(?Color?))

You need to specify a response= argument and a reference= argument. In
particular, a response= argument shifts ergm() into the valued mode,
enabling statistics like sum() and nonzero(). Take a look at
example(zach) in the ergm.count package and the tutorial linked above.

> Also, the only paper in my field to utilize ergm.count lists that both
> ?sum? and ?nonzero? were used in the same model. However, in the help
> file, it appears these are two different options for the form object -
> can someone please clarify this?

Sum models the overall average count, while nonzero models tendency to
have too many or too few zeros. They can both be in the model at the
same time. In particular, if you have a Poisson-reference ERGM with both
nonzero and sum terms in it, you get a form of the zero-modified
Poisson.

              I hope this helps,
              Pavel
